exercise.name: Weighted Crunch
steps: Lie face up with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a plate or dumbbell on your chest with both hands.
Curl your shoulders up by squeezing your stomach, then lower slowly.
exercise.one_line_summary: Lying face up, knees bent about 90 deg, feet flat; one dumbbell held on the chest. The upper back curls up about 30 deg until the shoulder blades leave the floor, low back stays down, then lowers. Rectus abdominis is the target.

setup.target: Face up on the floor, low back resting on the floor.
setup.tolerance: pelvis flat; no arch under the low back
setup.why: A crunch curls the upper trunk only; the pelvis and low back stay down (curl, not sit-up).

setup.target: Knees bent about 90 deg, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart.
setup.tolerance: knee bend 80-100 deg; feet 0.2-0.3 m apart
setup.why: Bent knees keep the hip flexors (rectus femoris) quieter than straight-leg sit-ups; S1 found high rectus femoris EMG in the bent-knee sit-up, not the crunch.

setup.target: One dumbbell held flat on the middle of the chest with both hands, elbows bent and close to the ribs.
setup.tolerance: dumbbell on the sternum, not behind the head
setup.why: S2 loaded the crunch at 20-100% of 1RM; the load on the chest raises abdominal EMG. Library step 2.

movement.measure: deg of forward bend of the upper trunk off the floor; 0 = lying flat
movement.end: about 30 deg (shoulder blades just off the floor)
movement.path: Upper back rolls up, lower back stays on the floor; same path down, slow.
Does not move. Hips do not flex further; this is a crunch, not a sit-up.
Still. Feet stay flat on the floor.
Head moves with the trunk; chin is not yanked to the chest.

movement.measure: arm angles in the torso frame
movement.start: elev 14.5, plane -53, elbow 120 (hands on the chest)
movement.end: same (the weight rides with the chest)
movement.path: Arms do not move relative to the chest; they do not throw the weight up.

muscles.anatomy: Rectus abdominis, upper and lower parts
muscles.emg: Crunch is among the highest exercises for upper and lower RA (S1, abstract gives no %); RA rises with external load, most at 100% 1RM (S2).
muscles.role: Main mover: curls the rib cage toward the pelvis.
muscles.surface: The two vertical bands down the front of the belly, from the lower ribs/breastbone to the pubic bone, either side of the midline.

muscles.emg: Crunch is among the highest for external and internal oblique in S1; S2 measured EO rising with load (no % in abstract).
muscles.role: Helps the curl and holds the trunk straight; not the target, so not lit.
muscles.surface: Sides of the waist from the lower ribs to the hip bone.

muscles.emg: Low in the crunch compared with the bent-knee sit-up (S1).
muscles.role: Holds the bent legs; should stay quiet.
muscles.surface: Front of the hip and thigh.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Low back leaves the floor and the trunk passes ~45 deg.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Turns it into a sit-up: hip flexors take over (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Chin jammed into the chest while the shoulders barely move.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Strains the neck; the abs do little.

sources.citation: Escamilla RF, McTaggart MS, Fricklas EJ, et al. 2006. An electromyographic analysis of commercial and common abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 36(2):45-57. doi:10.2519/jospt.2006.36.2.45
sources.what_it_gave: Crunch among the highest for upper/lower RA and obliques; rectus femoris highest in bent-knee sit-up, not the crunch.

sources.citation: Moraes AC, Pinto RS, Valamatos MJ, et al. 2009. EMG activation of abdominal muscles in the crunch exercise performed with different external loads. Phys Ther Sport 10(2):57-62. doi:10.1016/j.ptsp.2009.01.001
sources.what_it_gave: Crunch at 20-100% 1RM: RA and EO activation rise with load, greatest at 100%.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Crunch and curl-up data across studies (crunch highest IO of traditional exercises; curl-up IO ~62% MVIC).
